name: vision_keras_cnn_bad
title: The same Keras CNN with five planted defects
origin: domain-vision round 1: the dirty twin of vision_keras_cnn

expected.defect: the base dataset is shuffled and then split with take/skip, with reshuffle_each_iteration left at its default
expected.why: tf.data re-draws the buffer every epoch, so the validation rows swap with the training rows on every pass and the holdout stops existing from epoch two

expected.defect: the output layer carries activation="softmax" while the loss is SparseCategoricalCrossentropy(from_logits=True)
expected.why: the softmax is applied twice, so the gradient is tiny and the reported accuracy metric is computed on a distribution the loss never saw

expected.defect: the fine-tuning head returned by build_finetune_model() is fitted without ever being compiled
expected.why: an uncompiled model has no optimizer and no loss, so the call raises the moment it is reached - after the first model has already trained for thirty epochs
expected.gap: MLV705 is deliberately a workspace-wide claim (r_framework.py:156-171): it fires only when NO compile() exists anywhere. compile_model() compiles the first model, so the second, genuinely uncompiled model returned by build_finetune_model() can never be reported.

expected.defect: nothing seeds TensorFlow, numpy or Python; the seed= on the shuffle covers the shuffle alone
expected.why: the augmentation draw and the weight initialisation move between runs, so two runs of the same script are not comparable

forbidden.why: the shuffle that creates the split does carry seed=SEED - the defect is the ordering, not the seed

gaps.what: the augment map is applied to the validation and test datasets, so the held-out images are randomly flipped and colour-jittered - MLV114 covers torchvision and albumentations only, not a tf.data .map of a random tf.image op
the fine-tuning head is also built with activation='softmax' and, once compiled, would carry the same from_logits contradiction - MLV709 reports the first head only
